claims.text: Applying a short-duration, low-temperature heat treatment after each deposited AlCrFeNiSi layer will significantly reduce residual thermal stress.
The interlayer heat treatment will produce a more uniform metastable microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi.
The interlayer heat treatment will improve AlCrFeNiSi mechanical properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Standard high-thermal-load additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi produces high residual thermal stresses.
Standard high-thermal-load additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi produces non-uniform grain structures.
Standard high-thermal-load additive manufacturing degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi.
A build-plate temperature of approximately 600 °C and an effective dwell of approximately 10 minutes per layer constitute an applicable treatment window for AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed treatment window is applicable to laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi components with characteristic dimensions below 10 mm.
The treatment will refine the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure and make its grain-size distribution more uniform.
The treatment will reduce epitaxial columnar grain growth in AlCrFeNiSi.
Controlled lower-temperature interlayer heating minimizes steep thermal gradients during solidification.
Lower thermal gradients permit residual-stress relaxation in AlCrFeNiSi.
Controlled phase evolution and metastable-phase formation will prevent excessive grain coarsening.
The treated specimens will have lower XRD-measured residual stress than conventionally processed specimens.
The treated specimens will have increased yield strength.
The treated specimens will have increased ductility.
The intervention may become less effective for larger builds or geometries that exacerbate thermal gradients.
The optimum treatment temperature and duration are specific to the AlCrFeNiSi composition.
